en.g: Turn verbs and adjectives into nouns with common suffixes.
p: Adjective + -ness: happy to happiness, kind to kindness, dark to darkness (y changes to i).
Verb + -ment: improve to improvement, enjoy to enjoyment, agree to agreement.
Verb + -tion/-ation: inform to information, decide to decision, invite to invitation. Spelling can change.
en.q: What brings you the most happiness in daily life? Try to use two nouns with -ness, -ment or -tion.
en.c: Make nouns from ten words: kind, sad, develop, pay, educate, create, weak, move, relax, ill. Use three in sentences.

de.g: Mit typischen Endungen machst du aus Verben und Adjektiven Nomen.
p: Adjektiv + -ness: happy zu happiness, kind zu kindness, dark zu darkness (y wird zu i).
Verb + -ment: improve zu improvement, enjoy zu enjoyment, agree zu agreement.
Verb + -tion/-ation: inform zu information, decide zu decision, invite zu invitation. Die Schreibung kann sich ändern.
de.q: Was macht dich im Alltag am glücklichsten? Benutze zwei Nomen mit -ness, -ment oder -tion.
de.c: Bilde Nomen aus zehn Wörtern: kind, sad, develop, pay, educate, create, weak, move, relax, ill. Drei davon in Sätzen.

es.c: Forma sustantivos de diez palabras: kind, sad, develop, pay, educate, create, weak, move, relax, ill. Usa tres en frases.

en.g: Change the meaning of words with common prefixes.
p: Opposites: un- (unhappy, unusual), dis- (dislike, disagree), in-/im- (incorrect, impossible).
Re- means again: redo, rewrite, rebuild, reconsider. Can you repeat that? I need to restart my phone.
Mis- means wrongly: misunderstand, misspell, mislead. Sorry, I misunderstood the question.
en.q: What is something you dislike doing, and something you think is impossible to learn quickly?
en.c: Add a prefix to ten words: happy, agree, possible, write, understand, polite, appear, use, visible, connect. Use four.

en.g: Tell the difference between how you feel (-ed) and what causes it (-ing).
p: -ed describes feelings: I'm bored. She was interested. We were tired after the trip.
-ing describes the thing or person that causes the feeling: The film was boring. The talk was interesting.
Careful: I'm boring means people find you dull! Pairs: excited/exciting, surprised/surprising, relaxed/relaxing.
en.q: What was the most interesting thing you did last month, and when did you last feel really excited?
en.c: Write five pairs: one -ed and one -ing sentence each, with tired, amazed, confused, relaxed and embarrassed.

de.g: Du unterscheidest, wie du dich fühlst (-ed) und was das Gefühl auslöst (-ing).
p: -ed beschreibt Gefühle: I'm bored. She was interested. We were tired after the trip.
-ing beschreibt, was das Gefühl auslöst: The film was boring. The talk was interesting.
Vorsicht: I'm boring heißt, du bist langweilig! Paare: excited/exciting, surprised/surprising, relaxed/relaxing.
de.q: Was war das Interessanteste, das du letzten Monat gemacht hast, und wann warst du zuletzt richtig aufgeregt?

en.g: Use extreme adjectives with absolutely to sound more natural and expressive.
p: Normal and strong: big/huge, cold/freezing, tired/exhausted, good/fantastic, tasty/delicious, small/tiny.
With strong adjectives use absolutely or really: absolutely delicious, really exhausted. Not very delicious.
With normal adjectives use very or extremely: very cold, extremely tired. Completely also goes with strong ones.
en.q: Describe your best meal ever and the hottest or coldest day you remember, using strong adjectives.
en.c: Rewrite five plain sentences with strong adjectives: The room was big > The room was absolutely huge.

Zu starken Adjektiven passt absolutely oder really: absolutely delicious, really exhausted. Nicht very delicious.
Zu normalen Adjektiven passt very oder extremely: very cold, extremely tired. Completely geht mit starken.

en.g: Learn words that naturally go together, so your English sounds fluent.
p: Make: a decision, a mistake, a plan, friends, an effort. Do: homework, the shopping, exercise, your best.
Take: a photo, a break, a shower, a taxi. Catch: a cold, a bus, someone's attention.
Adjective + noun: heavy rain, strong coffee, a close friend, a busy street, fast food.

en.g: Talk about friends with common phrasal verbs.
p: Get on (well) with = have a good relationship: I get on really well with my cousin.
Fall out (with) = argue and stop being friends; make up = become friends again: We fell out but made up the next day.
Catch up = share news after time apart; hang out = spend free time together: Let's hang out and catch up!
en.q: Who do you get on really well with, and who would you love to catch up with soon?
en.c: Write a short story about two friends using get on with, fall out, make up, catch up and hang out.

Catch up = Neuigkeiten austauschen; hang out = Zeit zusammen verbringen: Let's hang out and catch up!

en.g: Use common phrasal verbs you hear in the office.

en.g: Understand and use common idioms at the right moment.
p: Piece of cake = very easy. Under the weather = a bit unwell. The test was a piece of cake!
Break the ice = make people relax at first meeting. Hit the books = study hard. A game broke the ice.
Use idioms in relaxed conversation, not in formal writing. One or two are enough to sound natural.
en.q: What was a piece of cake for you this week, and what is a good way to break the ice with new people?
en.c: Write a mini chat between two friends using four idioms: piece of cake, under the weather, break the ice, hit the books.

de.g: Du verstehst häufige Redewendungen und setzt sie im richtigen Moment ein.

Redewendungen passen zu lockeren Gesprächen, nicht zu formellen Texten. Ein oder zwei reichen völlig.
de.q: Was war diese Woche für dich kinderleicht, und wie bricht man gut das Eis mit neuen Leuten?
de.c: Schreib einen Mini-Chat zwischen zwei Freunden mit vier Redewendungen: piece of cake, under the weather, break the ice, hit the books.

es.c: Escribe un mini chat entre dos amigos con cuatro modismos: piece of cake, under the weather, break the ice, hit the books.

en.g: Recap narrative tenses, conditionals, reported speech and deduction.
p: Stories: I was walking home when I saw an old friend. I hadn't seen him for years. We've been chatting ever since.

Reporting and guessing: She said she was tired. He asked if I was free. They must have left. It can't be true.
